title: The extinction of a group is generally slower than its origination

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The extinction of a group is generally slower than its origination

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The complete extinction of the species of a group generally takes longer than their production, so a group's diversity tapers more gradually at its end than at its beginning, though some groups such as ammonites ended suddenly.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: There is reason to believe that the complete extinction of the species of a group is generally a slower process than their production

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “On Extinction”. Scope: genera, families and higher groups in the fossil record

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted temporal asymmetry is explicit and estimable across many fossil clades. Data biases remain, but existing records and sensitivity analyses can resolve the general tendency.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For many clades, compare the duration and slope of diversity accumulation after origin with decline before extinction, correcting for sampling. Test whether extinction phases are generally longer and more gradual than origination phases.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mass extinctions may dominate terminal slopes.

Boundary choice and time-bin width affect apparent asymmetry.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Rise and fall durations are computable from public richness curves for many marine groups. The principal sampling bias manufactures slower-looking extinctions, so an uncorrected asymmetry would not distinguish the claim from an artefact. Corrected analyses can be done for well-sampled clades and remain ambiguous for the general case.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each genus or family, compare the time from first appearance to the diversity peak with the time from the peak to last appearance. Systematically longer declines would support the claim; equal or shorter declines, once sampling bias is accounted for, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The Signor-Lipps effect lengthens apparent declines, which is the same direction as the claim.

How a group is delimited changes the measured durations of its rise and fall.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Extinct animal families in the fossil record are bottom-heavy: their genus diversity peaks early in their history and tapers over a longer decline, so the centre of gravity of the diversity trajectory lies in the first half of the family's duration.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: All 79,166 accepted Metazoa genera were fetched from the PBDB taxa API; genera without ages or family were dropped. A family was taken as extinct when none of its genera is flagged extant and none has a last appearance at 0 Ma. Each genus ranges through from firstapp_max_ma to lastapp_min_ma; genus diversity D(t) was counted on a 0.1 Myr grid between the family's first origin and final extinction, and the centre of gravity CG of D over relative time (0 = origin, 1 = extinction) was computed for the 1,866 extinct families with >= 5 genera and >= 10 Myr duration. The median CG, the share below 0.5 and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of CG - 0.5 were compared with the pre-registered thresholds; families ending within 2 Myr of the five big mass extinctions and families by era of origin are reported separately.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: from the Paleobiology Database taxa API, all accepted animal (Metazoa) genera with first and last appearance ages and family assignment. A family is extinct if none of its genera is flagged extant and every genus has lastapp_min_ma > 0. Each genus ranges from firstapp_max_ma to lastapp_min_ma; the family's range is the union. Diversity D(t) = number of genera ranging through t on a 0.1 Myr grid. Centre of gravity CG = sum(D(t) * tau(t)) / sum(D(t)), tau = (family origin - t) / (family origin - family end), so CG < 0.5 means diversity is concentrated early and decline is slower than rise. Families qualify with >= 5 genera and duration >= 10 Myr. SUPPORTS if the median CG < 0.5, the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of CG - 0.5 < 0 has p < 0.01, and at least 55% of families have CG < 0.5.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: REFUTES if the median CG >= 0.5. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 100 qualifying families: inconclusive (underpowered); PBDB API unreachable: inconclusive (data-unavailable). Descriptive secondary statistics: median CG and share below 0.5 for families ending at the five big mass extinctions (end-Ordovician 443.8, Late Devonian 372.2, end-Permian 251.9, end-Triassic 201.4, end-Cretaceous 66.0 Ma, within 2 Myr) versus all others, and for Paleozoic-, Mesozoic- and Cenozoic-originating families.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: median centre of gravity of range-through genus diversity of extinct animal families (0 = origin, 1 = extinction; < 0.5 = slow decline)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'complete extinction of the species of a group is generally a slower process than their production' is read through clade shape (Gould et al. 1977): if production is fast and extermination slow, the diversity trajectory rises steeply and tapers, giving a centre of gravity in the first half of the clade's duration. Groups are extinct animal families as classified in PBDB (Darwin's 'groups' of genera and families); diversity is counted in genera, because Darwin's species are rarely resolved in the fossil record. Range-through ranges from database first and last appearances are used without sampling correction; the Signor-Lipps effect pulls last appearances earlier and can shorten or lengthen the tail, so the test measures the record as compiled.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Paleobiology Database data service 1.2, taxa/list: accepted Metazoa genera with first and last appearance ages (show=app) and classification (show=class)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The asymmetry is real but small: median CG 0.477 (IQR 0.41-0.55), 59% of families below 0.5. It holds in every large phylum (Chordata 0.485, Arthropoda 0.473, Mollusca 0.462, Brachiopoda 0.489, Echinodermata 0.456, Cnidaria 0.473) and in Paleozoic-, Mesozoic- and Cenozoic-originating families (0.477, 0.482, 0.475). The test passes the pre-registered thresholds, but 'generally a slower process' is supported only as a modest tendency, not a strong rule.

As Darwin himself noted for ammonites, families ending at the big five mass extinctions are the exception: their median CG is 0.523 and only 41% are below 0.5 (n = 359), against 0.468 and 64% for families ending at other times (n = 1,507).

No sampling correction was applied. Range-through ranges from database first and last appearances are affected by the Signor-Lipps effect (last appearances drawn earlier); the 'pull of the Recent' does not apply because only extinct families are used. The grok assessor warned that sampling bias can manufacture slow-looking declines; the opposite bias (late-Lazarus truncation) also exists, so the direction of net bias is not known.

Genus first and last appearance ages are taken at the outer bounds of the first and last intervals (firstapp_max_ma, lastapp_min_ma), which lengthens every genus range by up to one interval at each end symmetrically.

Families are PBDB's classification, which includes paraphyletic families; Darwin's 'group' could also be read at the order or class level, which was not tested.

PBDB is a live database; re-running reproduces the method but counts drift as records are added.
